headlines.title: Trump’s pick for agency providing election security says Jan. 6 was not an attack
headlines.description: The nominee selected by President Donald Trump to lead the agency tasked with protecting elections in the U.S. refused Thursday to answer who won the 2020 presidential election or call the riot on Jan. 6, 2021, “an attack.”

headlines.title: Justice Department seeks dismissal of its lawsuit in Alaska Senate race
headlines.description: The Trump administration had sought to block certification of the election results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan lost. Democrat Mary Peltola won the race.

headlines.title: National cyber director to leave Trump administration
headlines.description: A White House official says Sean Cairncross will leave his position as National Cyber Director. The news comes as the country has been dealing with a series of tech outages. NBC News’ Stephanie Gosk reports.

headlines.title: Trump’s historic summit with Xi, Putin
headlines.description: President Trump held a historic trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia. NBC Nightly News anchor Tom Llamas reports.

headlines.title: Trump’s pick to lead election security agency says Jan. 6 was not an ‘attack’
headlines.description: Michael LoSapio, President Trump’s pick to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said that the riot on Jan. 6, 2021 was not an “attack,” when pressed by Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn. LoSapio also did not answer questions from Blumenthal on the outcome of the 2020 popular vote, which President Joe Biden won.

headlines.title: How the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner chaos unfolded
headlines.description: Secret Service faced challenges evacuating President, Vice President, Cabinet officials and Congressional leaders after gunman rushes D.C. gala.

headlines.title: White House national cyber director is leaving the administration
headlines.description: Sean Cairncross has played a key role in crafting AI policy for the Trump administration. His immediate replacement is Kirsten A. Davies.

headlines.title: Trump gives posthumous pardon to Pete Rose, all-time MLB hits leader
headlines.description: The baseball great, who died in 2024, pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been banned from the sport for betting on games.

headlines.title: Trump’s symbolic summit: From the Politics Desk
headlines.description: In today’s edition, Andrea Mitchell dives into the fallout from President Donald Trump’s trilateral meeting in China.

headlines.title: Classified NSA network is still down, leaving some staff working from home
headlines.description: The network went down on Tuesday due to a technical problem during maintenance operations, but sources say it has not affected its work collecting electronic intelligence.

headlines.title: Elon Musk says he is ‘not MAGA’ after spending millions on Trump and his allies
headlines.description: Elon Musk struck a more moderate tone while discussing his political affiliation Wednesday, arguing that he does not have “blind adherence” to the policies of the Republican Party or MAGA.

headlines.title: Sen. Elissa Slotkin fires back at DOJ official’s ‘sham’ investigation
headlines.description: U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz has suggested that Slotkin’s comments about congressional oversight could amount to a criminal civil rights offense.
